Monday's Mississippi headlines: a fatal shooting investigation in Horn Lake, a sheriff's warning about a jury-duty phone scam, a major grocery sale in Iuka, statewide school rankings, and preseason honors for a Mississippi State linebacker. Here is your evening roundup for Monday, October 12, 2026.

Top Stories

Horn Lake Shooting Leaves One Dead; Man Faces Murder Warrant

Horn Lake police say a shooting at Kabuki restaurant left Justin Conrad dead and led to a murder warrant for Marterius McShane.

Panola County Sheriff Warns of Jury-Duty Warrant Phone Scam

The Panola County Sheriff's Office is warning residents about calls claiming people have warrants for missing jury duty and demanding payment over the phone. If you get one of these calls, hang up and call the sheriff's office directly.

Prentiss County Sheriff's Office Investigates Burglary at District Shed

The Prentiss County Sheriff's Office is investigating an Oct. 10 burglary at a district shed and is seeking tips about the suspect and a work truck.

Brooks Grocery in Iuka Sold to Houchens Food Group

Brooks Grocery in Iuka has been acquired by Kentucky-based, employee-owned Houchens Food Group, a major ownership change for the local grocery scene.

Around the State

Oxford School District Ranked No. 5 in Mississippi in Niche's 2027 Rankings

The Oxford School District placed fifth in the state in Niche's 2027 rankings, with its elementary schools among the state's top 10.

Jeremy Hudson of Corinth to Join District Attorney's Office as Assistant DA

Jeremy Hudson of Corinth is set to join the District Attorney's office as an Assistant District Attorney.

Southaven's Fifth Annual FallFest Draws Vendors and 25+ Steak Cookoff Teams

Southaven's fifth annual FallFest drew vendors and more than 25 steak cook-off teams for the city's fall celebration.

Sports

Mississippi State's Josh Hubbard Named Preseason All-SEC First Team

Mississippi State linebacker Josh Hubbard was named to the Preseason All-SEC First Team by league media, a preseason honor for the Bulldogs' defense.

Mississippi News Report is published twice daily by the Mississippi News Group. Read more Mississippi news at msnewsgroup.com.

content.raw:
Good morning, Mississippi. The DeSoto County Sheriff's Office is asking for the public's help finding Zachery Pitcock, wanted in an aggravated assault case and considered armed and dangerous in the Pine Lake area. Gautier police are searching for 16-year-old Colten Potter, missing since he was last seen leaving the Bayou Oaks Street area. And on the courts, Ole Miss tennis is on a tear at the ITA Regionals, with a men's doubles title already in hand and a singles final berth on the women's side.

Top Stories

  • Zachery Pitcock wanted in aggravated assault case: The DeSoto County Sheriff's Office says Pitcock is considered armed with knives and dangerous, and was last seen in the Pine Lake area. Read more on DeSoto County News.
  • Gautier police seek help locating 16-year-old Colten Potter: Police are asking for information about the 16-year-old, last seen leaving the Bayou Oaks Street area. Read more on Mississippi News Group.
  • Tupelo police announce felony shoplifting arrest: Tupelo police announced a felony shoplifting arrest involving Best Buy, with the case set for presentation to the Lee County Grand Jury. Read more on Mississippi News Group.

Around Mississippi

  • Mississippi community briefing: Mississippi News Group's Oct. 12 community briefing rounds up the day's verified local updates with dates, places, and source links for each item. Read the briefing on Mississippi News Group.
  • A first timer's perspective on the Mississippi State Fair: Claudia Amendoeira writes for Mississippi Today on her first trip to the fair — "all's fair in love and biscuits." Read more on DeSoto County News.
  • NEMCC, Delta State nursing students present at Destin conference: Nursing students from Northeast Mississippi Community College and Delta State presented their projects at a conference in Destin. Read more on Alcorn County News.

Sports

  • Ole Miss tennis collects ITA Regional hardware: Ole Miss women's tennis player Alice Battesti advanced to the singles final at the ITA Regional Championships, and the Rebel men's team captured the doubles title. Battesti's run and the doubles championship on Mississippi Sports.
  • Ole Miss women's golf fourth after two rounds at Illini Invitational: The 20th-ranked Rebel women sit fourth after two rounds in Illinois. Read more on Mississippi Sports.
  • Monday night's high school slate: State-final berths and a softball decider headlined Monday night's Mississippi high school schedule. See the Games to Watch preview on Mississippi Sports.

content.raw:
Trick-or-treat night in Tippah County is serious business — from Ripley's neighborhoods to the country roads, the porch lights are on and the kids are out in force. Whether you're stocking up for the trick-or-treat rush, filling classroom treat bags, or handing out at the trunk-or-treat, buying candy in bulk beats paying full price bag-by-bag. Tippah County families go through a lot of candy every October, and we rounded up five well-reviewed bulk candy and treat packs on Amazon that cover every doorbell you'll hear.

As an Amazon Associate we earn from qualifying purchases.

Prices below were checked on 2026-10-13 and can change — click through for today's price.

Why Tippah County Families Love Bulk Halloween Candy

Every Tippah County parent knows the math: buy the small bag and you're back at the store Thursday night; buy the bulk bag and you're done for the season. These five packs cover the whole crowd — chocolate lovers, gummy fans, kids with allergies, and the little ones who need something softer. All individually wrapped, all ready for the bowl by the front door.

1. SNICKERS, SKITTLES Gummies, TWIX & LIFE SAVERS 160-Count Variety Pack

The one-bag answer: 160 individually wrapped pieces — a 4.15-pound bulk bag mixing chocolate (Snickers, Twix, Milky Way) with gummies (Skittles Gummies, Life Savers Gummies). Chocolate kids get their favorites, gummy kids get theirs, and #15 in Chocolate Candy Variety Packs means it's a proven crowd-pleaser.

Key specs:
160 individually wrapped fun-size and mini pieces, 4.15 lb bulk bag
Chocolate (Snickers, Twix, Milky Way) plus Skittles and Life Savers gummies
~4.4 stars with ~290 reviews; #15 in Chocolate Candy Variety Packs

Price: ~$25 as of 2026-10-13

Check price on Amazon

2. Airheads 90 Full-Size Candy Bars Variety Box

The upgrade pick: 90 FULL-size Airheads bars, individually wrapped in 6 fruit flavors — the house on the street that hands out full-size bars gets remembered. Peanut-free and tree nut free, gluten free, kosher, and non-melting, so it's a safe bet for classroom bags too.

Key specs:
90 full-size individually wrapped bars in 6 fruit flavors
Peanut-free, tree nut free, gluten free, and kosher; non-melting
Mirrored listing shows 439 reviews — a well-liked variety box

Price: ~$13.59 as of 2026-10-13 (Prime deal noted early October; click through for today's price)

Check price on Amazon

3. YumEarth Organic Halloween Variety Box, 50 Count

The allergy-friendly option: 50 Organic Pops, Gummy Fruits, and Giggles — top 9 allergen free, USDA Organic, non-GMO, vegan, with no artificial dyes or high-fructose corn syrup. Every year more families hand out a bowl that every kid can eat from, and this is the box that makes it easy.

Key specs:
50 pieces: Organic Pops, Gummy Fruits, and Giggles
Top 9 allergen free — USDA Organic, non-GMO, vegan, no artificial dyes or HFCS
4.65/5 from 95 reviews; #72 in Gummy Candies

Price: ~$29 as of 2026-10-13

Check price on Amazon

4. Halloween Fruit Snacks Variety Pack, 80 Count

The non-candy crowd-pleaser: 80 individually wrapped fruit snacks (64 oz) — peanut-free, fat-free, no high-fructose corn syrup, with 100% daily Vitamin C. Halal and a hit with the 600+ buyers who picked it up this past month; a smart pick for classroom treat bags where candy isn't allowed.

Key specs:
80 individually wrapped packs, 64 oz total
Peanut-free, fat-free, no HFCS, 100% daily Vitamin C; halal
600+ bought in the past month; #89 in Fruit Snacks

Price: ~$23 as of 2026-10-13

Check price on Amazon

5. Rice Krispies Treats Halloween Pack, 60 Bars

The classroom classic: 60 bite-size crispy mini marshmallow squares in festive Halloween packaging — no HFCS, and the small size is just right for younger trick-or-treaters and school parties. #58 in Breakfast Cereal Bars and rated 4.4/5 by buyers.

Key specs:
60 individually wrapped bite-size bars, 23.2 oz box
Festive Halloween packaging; no high-fructose corn syrup
4.4/5 buyer rating; #58 in Breakfast Cereal Bars

Price: ~$10.88 as of 2026-10-13

Check price on Amazon

Buying Guide: Stocking Up on Halloween Treats

Count the doorbell rings. A busy Ripley street can see 150+ trick-or-treaters — the 160-count variety bag covers one night with room to spare. Rural routes need less; order accordingly.

Mix candy with a non-candy option. Pairing a chocolate bag with fruit snacks or Rice Krispies Treats covers the kids with allergies and the parents who'd rather see fewer sweets.

Go allergy-friendly for shared bowls. Peanut-free and top-9-free options like Airheads, YumEarth, and fruit snacks mean nobody has to sit a bowl out. It matters more every year.

Check the date. Individually wrapped bulk candy keeps fine through the season, but buy fresh for the best taste — and store it cool so the chocolate doesn't bloom before the 31st.

Order before the rush. Candy prices climb and bulk bags sell out the week before Halloween. Order this week and you're stocked for trick-or-treat night, the school party, and the trunk-or-treat too.

From the Ripley square to the Tippah County back roads, one good bulk order keeps the candy bowl full all season. Any of these five will get it done — grab yours before the Halloween rush.

Read every label. “Peanut-free” and “top-nine-allergen-free” do not mean suitable for every allergy. FARE recommends checking each treat’s label, including mini and fun-size versions, and avoiding treats without ingredient labels. Parents or caregivers should review treats before children eat them.

Check the date. Individually wrapped bulk candy keeps fine through the season, but buy fresh for the best taste — and store it cool so the chocolate doesn't bloom before the 31st.

Order before the rush. Candy prices climb and bulk bags sell out the week before Halloween. Order this week and you're stocked for trick-or-treat night, the school party, and the trunk-or-treat too.

From the Ripley square to the Tippah County back roads, one good bulk order keeps the candy bowl full all season. Any of these five will get it done — grab yours before the Halloween rush.

Correction (Oct. 13, 2026): Earlier wording incorrectly implied these treats were suitable for every child or allergy. Rice Krispies Treats Original Mini Squares include milk and soy ingredients. Check each current package’s ingredients and allergen statement.

Today in Tippah County comes down to four things: Walnut volleyball playing for a state championship berth tonight, one more day of near-record heat before a sharp cold front arrives Friday, the rescheduled Walnut Firehouse 5K on Saturday, and Mississippi's Fall Severe Weather Preparedness Week, which begins today.

Walnut Volleyball Plays for a State Berth Tonight

The Walnut Lady Wildcats (31-4) travel to East Union High School in Blue Springs for the North State final at 6 p.m. Their opponent is unbeaten East Union (36-0), which beat Walnut 3-1 when the teams met Sept. 1. Walnut comes in on a 12-match winning streak and has swept all three of its playoff opponents, most recently Myrtle last Thursday. Our North State final preview has the details, and TippahSports.com also has a preview of the rematch.

Walnut is the only Tippah County volleyball team still playing. Ripley, Pine Grove and Falkner have finished their seasons. Walnut and Falkner are set to combine into North Tippah High School after the 2026-27 school year, so this group is among the last to play under the Walnut High School name. The winner advances to the state championship. We will post the result after the match.

Heat Holds Through Thursday, Then a Cold Front

If you are heading to Blue Springs tonight, expect warm weather. The National Weather Service in Memphis has Ripley near 90 today, near 91 on Tuesday and near 92 on Wednesday and Thursday, with overnight lows in the low 60s. Forecasters said the region is flirting with potential record-breaking warmth through at least Thursday. Little or no rain is expected in Tippah County this week.

The pattern changes late Thursday into Friday. Our Tippah County cold front report shows the current Ripley forecast at a high near 78 on Friday, near 69 on Saturday and near 74 on Sunday, with lows in the 40s. Keep a jacket handy for Saturday morning, and consider bringing in tender plants if lows trend colder.

The cooler air will not end the dry spell. The U.S. Drought Monitor map released Oct. 8 shows all of Tippah County in at least moderate drought, with about 46 percent of the county in severe drought. Supervisors extended the burn ban through Oct. 18 and are expected to decide on any further extension at their Oct. 15 meeting, as we reported in Sunday's roundup. Please skip outdoor burning until then.

Severe Weather Preparedness Week Starts Today

Gov. Tate Reeves declared Oct. 12-17 Fall Severe Weather Preparedness Week, according to our report based on SuperTalk Mississippi. The governor's office noted that tornadoes can happen in October, November and December, and that Mississippi recorded seven between October and December last year. The Mississippi Emergency Management Agency and the National Weather Service will share one topic each day: make a plan today, severe thunderstorms Tuesday, tornado safety Wednesday, flash flooding Thursday and warning reception methods Friday. No severe weather is expected in Tippah County this week, which makes it a good time to sort out where your family would go and how you would get warnings.

Walnut Firehouse 5K Is Saturday

The Walnut Firehouse 5K, the Walnut Volunteer Fire Department's biggest fundraiser, was moved from Oct. 10 to Saturday, Oct. 17 at 8:30 a.m. because of forecast heavy rain. The race is open to runners and walkers, and every dollar goes to the department. The flyer lists a USATF-certified course, door prizes, a medallion for every finisher and shirts guaranteed for the first 100 participants. Registration is $25, and race-day sign-in was listed as 7 to 8:20 a.m. Check the Walnut Fire & Rescue Facebook page for updates. The 5K follows Walnut's senior night football game against Hamilton on Friday, Oct. 16.

Around the Network

Tupelo police arrested James Boullion, 20, of Walnut on Oct. 7 on a felony shoplifting charge from a Sept. 8 incident at the Best Buy on North Gloster Street, according to our report. A judge set bond at $2,500, and the case will go to the Lee County Grand Jury. A charge is not a conviction.

In Alcorn County, Alcorn News MS reports Corinth voters choose a mayor Tuesday, Oct. 13, from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. at Corinth City Hall. Also from Alcorn News, citing the Daily Corinthian, aldermen adopted an emergency ordinance Friday banning kratom sales in the city, which you can read about in their story. In DeSoto County, DeSoto County News has its own look at preparedness week and the weekend cold front.

More Local Coverage
